pr.title: Avatar: replace the Claude logo with a Bridge-drawn agent mark
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

The agent Avatar (`<Avatar kind="agent" brand="claude">`) shipped the Claude logo (simple-icons `siClaude` path and the Anthropic brand color `#D97757`) on a cream tile, inside the published `@bridge-ds/react`. Anthropic's trademark guidelines (anthropic.com/legal/trademark-guidelines, effective 2024-08-01) require prior approval for every use of their logos. Bridge now draws its own agent mark and ships no vendor logo anywhere.

Agent-authored (Claude Code), to be reviewed by the owner before merge. Do not publish to npm without the owner's OK: the release PR changesets opens afterwards stays unmerged.

### The mark

- A prompt chevron and a cursor line, drawn in the Field Guide line style (stroke in `currentColor`, round caps and joins, slightly hand-drawn quadratic curves, no fill). Not a face, not a sparkle, not any company's logo.
- Deep Harbor line (`color.action.primary.bg`, the same role the Field Guide drawings use for "deep") on a Harbor tile. Dark theme: the dark zone tile with the light Deep Harbor line. Contrast = the `action.primary.bg` on `bg.zone` pair the token build already checks (7.03 light, 9.60 dark, ocean 4.81).
- A rounded square (`radius.inset`) instead of a circle, so an agent never reads as a person at a glance, even in a group next to illustrated faces on the same Harbor color (GitHub draws apps and bots the same way).
- Mark box per size on the size scale: 16, 20, 24, 28px for xs, sm, md, lg (line 1.5 to 2.5px).
- Explored six glyphs next to illustrated faces at every size (prompt, drafting divider, node graph, cursor, trail with flag, loop). Rejected: the divider reads as an "A" (too close to an Anthropic monogram), nodes read as "share", cursor reads as Figma, trail and loop are noise at 20px.

### API (non-breaking, minor)

- `kind="agent"` and `brand="claude"` unchanged; the accessible name stays "Claude AI".
- New `AGENT_MARK` export (`viewBox`, `path`, `strokeWidth`, `color`). `CLAUDE_MARK` stays exported as a `@deprecated` alias pointing to `AGENT_MARK`.
- New optional `mark?: ReactNode` (agents only): a vendor logo for teams who have the brand owner's approval. Documented in `Avatar.docs.json` guidance.
- The trademark code comment is rewritten.

### Every place the Claude logo, its color or the cream tile appeared

| Place | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx` | `CLAUDE_MARK` (siClaude path + `#D97757`), rendered as a fill | `AGENT_MARK` + deprecated alias, drawn mark, `mark` prop, new comment |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/index.ts` | exported `CLAUDE_MARK` | exports `AGENT_MARK` and `CLAUDE_MARK` |
| `packages/react/src/dom/avatar.ts` (`avatarHtml`, used by docs-site `scripts/people.ts`) | Claude path markup | agent mark markup (same as React, tested) |
| `packages/react/src/components/Avatar/Avatar.module.css` | cream tile, circle, mark 62% | Harbor rounded square, Deep Harbor line, sized mark box |
| `packages/tokens/src/semantic/{light,dark}.tokens.json` `color.agent.surface` | `{palette.warning.50}` cream in both themes | `{palette.primary.200}` light, `{palette.primary.900}` dark |
| `packages/tokens/src/brands/ocean.light.tokens.json` | (none) | `color.agent.surface` follows the ocean zone (`primary.50`) |
| `Avatar.docs.json` | "cream" anatomy, Claude mark wording | Bridge mark wording, `mark` guidance sentence, anatomy |
| `Avatar.stories.tsx` | "Claude mark on its cream tile" | Bridge mark; group story now mixes people and the agent at every size |
| `packages/react/component-specs.json` + Figma UI kit | no agent variant (kind "does not change the styles") | Kind axis person/agent, agent variants draw the mark as a vector bound to `color.action.primary.bg`, tile bound to `avatar.agent-bg` |
| `packages/core/src/node/component-specs.ts` | dropped `stroke-linejoin` | keeps it (the mark's chevron joins stay round in Figma) |
| `apps/figma-plugin/test/component-pull.test.ts` | `Size=md, Fallback=initials` | variant name with `Kind=person`, new assertions on the agent variant |
| docs-site uses (`faces.tsx`, `ComponentsList.tsx`, `LibraryEditMode.tsx`, `scripts/people.ts`) | rendered the logo through the Avatar | unchanged code, now render the Bridge mark |

Not found anywhere else: no Claude path in MCP, admin, docs json, snapshots or public assets. The name "Claude AI" is kept everywhere the agent is named.

Note for Figma: the Avatar set gains a `Kind` property. The agent variants exist for both Fallback values (the fallback does not apply to agents), 16 variants instead of 8.

## Risk tier

- [ ] Tier 1, low
- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [x] Tier 3, high: token value changed (`color.agent.surface`), new prop and export. Design + tech owner approval required

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`npm run lint:css` passes)
- [x] Semantic tokens used in components, not primitives
- [x] Checked in Storybook in **light and dark** themes
- [x] Accessibility: axe tests pass; the mark is decorative, the name is on the root
- [x] Stories updated (sizes, group mixing people and the agent at xs, sm, md, lg)
- [x] Changeset: minor `@bridge-ds/react`, patch tokens, core, figma-plugin
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted

## Checks run locally

typecheck, `npm test` (1708 passed), plugin tests (113 passed), mcp tests (134 passed), lint:css, audit:docs, specs check, build-storybook, docs:build.

## UI quality bar

Component-level change, no new screen. Studio home (light and dark, 1440) checked with real repo data: the agent tile sits in the greeting zone and in the row card; one primary action (Review) unchanged, no change to font sizes or interactive counts (page content and shell unchanged by this PR). Bridge brand: Deep Harbor is the only strong color in the mark, Harbor stays a zone color, no vendor color left.

## Screenshots

Local screenshots (Storybook AllStates and Agent stories, Studio home), light and dark, attached by the agent in its report.

pr.title: Avatar: illustrated faces and Claude's identity; Quality health header with Share
pr.author: peterbono
pr.body:
## What changed and why

Claude Code wrote this PR. The owner pre-approved the design and tech on 2026-10-19, including the new dependency. It is rebased on main after #136 (the new home and the review queue) #140 to #147 (the Branches page with its shared row component, the nav order and Figma coverage), and #150, #152 and #153 (the branch review and the reworked review queue). Do not merge: it waits for the owner.

### 1. DS Avatar (`@bridge-ds/react` minor, `@bridge-ds/tokens` minor)

| API | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fallback?: 'initials' \| 'illustrated'` (default `initials`) | `illustrated` shows a drawn face when there is no photo, or when the photo fails. The same `seed` always gives the same face. |
| `seed?: string` (default: the name) | Pass the login, so a renamed person keeps their face. |
| `illustration?: string` | A ready image for the illustrated fallback. Without it, `illustrated` shows initials. |
| `kind?: 'person' \| 'agent'` + `brand: 'claude'` | The Claude mark (orange `#D97757`, path from simple-icons `siClaude`) on a cream tile with a hairline edge. Same round shape as people. Accessible name "Claude AI". `name` is optional for the preset. |
| `@bridge-ds/react/avatar-illustrated` (new entry) | `Avatar` (fills `illustration` from the seed), `illustratedAvatarSvg(seed)`, `illustratedAvatarUri(seed)`. |
| `@bridge-ds/react/dom` | `avatarHtml(options)`. Same markup as the React Avatar, with a parity test. |

**How the faces are drawn**
- DiceBear "Notionists" style: design CC0 1.0 by Zoish, code MIT.
- Dependencies `@dicebear/core@9.4.3` and `@dicebear/collection@9.4.3`, pinned.
- Generated locally, no network. Only `notionists` is imported.
- No hands or body icons, and framed on the face (`scale` 125, `translateY` 12) so they read at 20 to 40px.
- The SVG is transparent; the tile colour comes from a token.
- Install note: `@dicebear/collection` also installs the other DiceBear styles, some of them CC BY 4.0. Only the CC0 Notionists drawings reach a bundle. To avoid installing them, `@dicebear/notionists` is a drop-in swap.

**Bundle impact**
- The drawings weigh 381 kB minified, about 122 kB gzipped. They live in the separate `./avatar-illustrated` entry, so the main entry stays light.
- Built package: `dist/index.js` and `dist/dom.js` contain no DiceBear code. `dist/avatar-illustrated.js` is 1.3 kB, plus a shared 5.6 kB Avatar chunk, because DiceBear stays an external dependency.
- The main entry grows by the Avatar code and the Claude path, about 3 kB raw.
- In Studio the drawings load on demand: a dynamic import after the first paint, as one 381 kB chunk. Pages that show no people never load them. The static Library examples draw at build time and ship no JavaScript.

**Tokens (tier 3, pre-approved)**
- `color.illustration.surface`: light is `palette.primary.200` (the Harbor zone colour). Dark is `palette.primary.300`, because the navy dark zone made the black lines vanish. Black lines are 16.6:1 on the light value and 13.4:1 on the dark one.
- `avatar.illustrated-bg` points to `color.illustration.surface`.
- `color.agent.surface` is `palette.warning.50`, cream, the same in both themes. `avatar.agent-bg` and `avatar.agent-border` (`color.border.default`) go with it.
- Contrast note: the Claude orange on the cream tile is 2.91:1. The mark is a decorative logo inside an element named "Claude AI", so it adds no contrast pair. `contrast.checks.json` is untouched.

**Docs and tests**
- Stories: Illustrated and Agent, plus `AllStates` rows for every size, a broken image, and a group mixing people and Claude.
- `Avatar.docs.json`: the Library examples draw at build time.
- Tests: the same seed gives the same face and a different seed a different one; the main entry falls back to initials; a failing image falls back to the drawing; the Claude preset has its accessible name, passes axe, and can be decorative; the `+N` counter names agents; the DOM renderer matches the React markup.
- Changeset: react minor, tokens minor, docs-site minor.

**Trademark:** the Claude logo is an Anthropic trademark, used here only to attribute actions Claude took. **The owner must check Anthropic's brand guidelines before release.**

### 2. Adoption in Studio

Faces and display names, through `scripts/people.ts`, `lib/people.ts` and `components/ds/studio/faces.ts`.

**Display names**
- Shown instead of "@login": in the change and history details, the conversation line, explorations, the history author filter, the release card ("can publish it"), and the who-acts sentences of a change (`markLogins`).
- Names come from the GitHub profile (`GET /users/:login`), cached for a week.
- Lookups per page view: 4 when anonymous, 20 when signed in. The viewer's own name comes free.
- With no profile name, the login shows without "@". No name is invented (peterbono has none).

**Faces** (the illustrated face, seeded by login, wherever there was no photo)
- Change rows, with ", by <name>" for screen readers.
- History rows and the history detail byline.
- Explorations.
- The new home: the "waiting on you" stack, the Needs you rows, and the reviewer on branch cards. This also removes the 12px and 10.5px initials font sizes on the home.
- The review queue, through the shared row component.
- Places that already showed a GitHub photo keep it: the change header and the conversation.

**Claude's identity**
- Shown on: Claude-made changes (`agentMade`: labels, body markers, Co-Authored-By), which read "Claude, with <name>"; history entries; explorations; the home "Claude AI" rows and stack; guidance drafts in Components ("Draft by Claude, needs review" with the mark in front); and the Library edit mode flags ("Drafted by Claude", "Claude proposes").

**Shared files touched (minimal edits)**
- `lib/changes.ts`: `CachedPull.agent`.
- `styles/site.css`: `.person`.
- `scripts/reviews.ts`, `scripts/history/page.ts`, `StudioHome.tsx`.

**Two fixes found on the way**
- History crashed ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')"): the DS Input ignores `id`, so `#hs-token` never existed. The page now finds the field by its datalist.
- The history detail showed the "Next release" zone (two Harbor zones) and a raw commit title. It now has one zone and the full human title (`historySummary(e, { full: true })`).

### 3. Quality page

**Header**
- Title with Share at the end of the title line, at both widths.
- One Harbor zone holding:
  - a verdict that names the single open finding: "Nothing blocks the library. VisuallyHidden guidance is a draft."
  - one primary, "Review guidance", full width on phones.
  - the three Library health cards, each linking to its section below: 0 failing contrast checks (304 checked in 2 brands, light and dark), 97.8% of components come from Bridge (up from 7.6%), and 52 of 53 components have reviewed guidance (1 drafted by Claude).
- Every number comes from the contrast gate (`lib/stats`), the committed audit reports and the guidance state. The page reads them through `lib/library-health.ts`, which has tests.

**Share** (a secondary button opening a DS Menu)
- Copy summary: copies the text below and announces "Summary copied. Paste it in Slack or on a slide.":
  ```
  Bridge library health
  Nothing blocks the library. VisuallyHidden guidance is a draft.

  - All 304 contrast checks pass in 2 brands, light and dark.
  - 97.8% of components in 2 products come from Bridge, up from 7.6% before Bridge.
  - 52 of 53 components have reviewed usage guidance: 1 drafted by Claude to review.

  Details: <origin>/studio/quality/
  ```
- Download image: `bridge-quality.png`, 1200x630 at 2x. It is an SVG built from the same numbers, with colours read from the page tokens (so it follows light or dark) and the page's latin Fraunces and Instrument Sans embedded. It is drawn on a canvas client side, with no new dependency. Verified in headless Chrome in both themes.


### After the #147 rebase

- **Shared row:** home and Branches now draw people through one shared `Who` (`components/ds/studio/faces.tsx`), used by both StudioHome and BranchesList as the `BranchRow` `who`. Both show the illustrated face when there is no photo, and Claude's identity on Claude-made work.
- **Display-name rule** (`lib/home-model` `shortName`, used by `displayName` and the greeting):
  - Use the first word of the GitHub profile name, unless it is an article (The, A, An, Le, La, Les) or shorter than 2 letters.
  - In that case use the full name ("The Octocat", "J. Doe"). With no profile name, use the login.
  - Unit tested.
- **Props shape:** `AvatarProps` is one interface again, so the docs tables and the Figma spec reader can read it. The component itself keeps the strict `AvatarPersonProps | AvatarAgentProps` type.
- **Component specs:** `component-specs.json` is regenerated. Avatar gains a Fallback axis. Its preview text now reads "?" instead of "FG", because the reader cannot evaluate the agent name fallback.


### Shared branch row (owner feedback, 2026-10-20)

`BranchRow` is used by the home Needs you list, the review queue and Branches.

- **Two fixed lines on every row:**
  - Line 1 is the title alone, on one line with an ellipsis. The full title is in the link's `title` attribute.
  - Line 2 is the optional Jira key in mono, the muted sentence, then the status pill right after it.
  - The " · " separator is gone.
- **Phones (390):** the sentence may wrap and the pill may go under it, inside the text block. The row button stays at the end, never between.
- **Rows without a person** (health, setup): the icon sits in the avatar's box, 32px round, on the initials avatar tile (`--avatar-bg`). It uses a plain glyph (TriangleAlert, Check) so it never draws a circle inside a circle, and the leading column aligns.
- **Screenshots:** a row with a long title, light and dark, at 1440, 1920 and 390: `it6-*` and `it7-*`.
- **Figma plugin test:** it now addresses the Avatar variant as `Size=md, Fallback=initials`, since the spec has the new Fallback axis.


### After the #152 rebase

- **Branch review (`BranchReview`):** the "who asks" header and every conversation entry draw people through the shared `Who`. That means the GitHub photo, else the illustrated face, and Claude as Claude, with names from the review's display-name map (never logins).
- **Review queue list:** each item shows the face of who waits on you (person or Claude) between the progress mark and the title.
- **Unchanged from main:** `scripts/reviews.ts` and `review-queue.css` keep main's new structure. My older string-built detail adoption was dropped with them, because main's React review replaced it.

### UI bar

- Screenshots: `scratchpad/avatar-quality/`, light and dark, 1440 and 390, iterations it1 to it4.
- Interactive elements on the first screen (page content / with shell):

  | Page | 1440 | 390 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Quality | about 12 / 25 | 6 / 12 |
  | Home | 8 / 23 | 4 / 8 |
  | Review queue | 5 / 20 | 6 / 10 |
  | History | 13 / 24 | 9 / 13 |
  | Explorations | 8 / 19 | 4 / 8 |
  | Components | 25 / 38 | 13 / 19 |
  | Changes, Merged filter | 27 / 38 | 24 / 28 |

  - Quality at 1440: the automatic count says 35 / 48, but that includes 23 hidden links of the footer "View source" menu.
  - Components and Changes are long lists: the count is mostly the rows themselves.
- Font sizes on the first screen: 3 or 4 everywhere. One exception: on Quality the existing AdoptionMetric value (21px) peeks in at the bottom of 1440.
- One Harbor zone per screen, one primary per view. No horizontal scroll at 390.
- No em dash, and no developer words added on first screens.

### Critique iterations (subagent critic)

1. **Iteration 1** found:
   - faces vanishing on the dark zone;

## What changed and why

### Asked fixes
1. **SegmentedControl, dark:** the selected segment's edge is `color.control.checked.bg`, the same edge as a pressed Button toggle (#118). Before, `border.default` matched the raised plate in dark, so there was no edge. The edge also shows in light (Deep Harbor on the white plate), which matches the Button toggle.
2. **Banner strong, dark:** new semantic `color.surface.strong` (`palette.primary.700` in both themes, so Deep Harbor). It replaces `action.primary.bg`, which is light blue in dark and read like a Harbor zone. Text and focus ring use `color.text.on-solid` (8.87:1 bridge, 7.39:1 ocean).

   - The merge method sits in a "For developers" fold, as a DS SegmentedControl. A DS Select can't be used: its portaled popup would be inert under the modal.

4. **All tokens:** the filter Input and the type SegmentedControl are both `md` (44px). A small SegmentedControl is 38px, against 32px for a small Input. The filter field is now full width on phones.
5. **Quality audit tables:** `narrowLayout="stack"` on the four report tables and on ContrastFailTable, with a `label` on each cell because the page is static. The `ad-scroll` wrappers are removed.

### Earlier critic findings, checked on main
- **Neutral Badge and grey status chips losing their fill in dark: fixed.** New `color.feedback.neutral.bg` (neutral.100 light, neutral.800 dark). `bg.subtle` is the card color in dark.
- **Combobox list barely separated from a Dialog in dark: fixed.** The `popup.border` component token is now `color.border.emphasis` (neutral.700 in dark). This applies to every popup.
- **Changes tab bar scrolling on phones: fixed.** The tab reads "All" at 480px and below, and the four tabs fit at 390.
- **Tokens filter chips with a near-black fill: fixed.** The selected chip uses `surface.selected` with the checked edge.
- **"Changed in this change" repeated on every row: fixed.** It is now "Changed", "New" or "Changed, dark theme only", since the banner already names the change.
- **Oversized "Bring in the latest library": fixed.** It was the DS `lg` (48px) and is now `md` (44px), the same as the other row actions.
- **"Your turn: fix tests": fixed.** The logic was wrong. The list chip told a designer author it was their turn, while the detail page said "Waiting for a developer… Your design is not the problem".
  - A new pure helper, `developerOnlyFailures` (lib/check-explain), classifies failing check names.
  - `whoActs` now gives developer-only failures to "a developer", with the chip "Blocked by tests". This applies to the list and the Overview.
  - A failing design rule stays the author's turn. Unit tests are added.
- **"N updates behind": fixed.** It now reads "Library moved on: N updates".
- **Native select in the Tokens Options sheet: already gone on main.** It is a BridgedSelect. Checked in the DOM: 0 `select`, 1 DS combobox.
- **Search palette result icon: fixed.** The colored chart-series dots are replaced by the side nav's DS Icons (page, component, token). Color tokens keep their swatch.
- **Studio overview hero action: kept, it meets the bar.** "Start a change" is a secondary Menu on the page title line (the page header action), with one primary in the to-do rows. At 390 it fills its bar.

| Token | Light | Dark | Contrast pair added |

pr.body:
## What changed and why

Bridge, the docs platform (`apps/docs-site`), is now built with the Bridge design system it documents (dogfooding). Agent-authored (Claude Code, lead agent plus parallel sub-agents on disjoint files), reviewed by nobody yet.

- **Tokens.** The chrome palette (Fog, Deck, Steel, Slate, International Orange, Cable) was the DS `bridge` brand with drifted values, so no third brand was needed. The scope menu only reaches preview surfaces (`data-preview-brand` / `data-preview-density`).
- **New tokens (Tier 3, owner asked).** These are DTCG, in both themes, with descriptions and a changeset:
  - `color.chart.series.1-6`, `color.chart.track`, `color.chart.grid` and `color.chart.axis`, on a new `palette.categorical` role (bridge: plum, ocean: orange).
  - `color.border.emphasis`.

  - `size.40` and `size.64`.
  - `font.size.900` and `font.size.1000`, for landing display only.

- **CSS.** All 20 docs stylesheets pass the same token-only stylelint rules as component CSS (the docs-site exemption is gone), plus `bridge/use-tokens`. 141 rules made dead by the swap are deleted. Global `kbd`, `table` and link rules no longer hit DS parts.
- **Components.** Controls render with `@bridge-ds/react`, statically by default; the vanilla scripts keep their id and `data-*` hooks. The components used are Button, IconButton, ButtonLink, Badge, Tag, Kbd, Alert, EmptyState, Input, Textarea, Select, Switch, Table, Breadcrumb, Link, Popover (the scope and version menus, `client:idle`) and the two new ones below.
- **New DS components (Tier 2).** Both are reused 3+ times and come with stories, `docs.json` and tests:
  - `SegmentedControl` (Forms) has a static HTML contract that a vanilla script can drive.
  - `PageHeader` (Layout).
- **Audit fixes (`@bridge-ds/core`, patch).**
  - A ring built only from tokens (`inset 0 0 0 var() var()`) is no longer counted as a hardcoded shadow.
  - `<Button render={<a href />}>` no longer counts the anchor as a separate native link.
- **Enforcement.** `lint:css` builds and runs `@bridge-ds/stylelint-plugin` on docs-site CSS. `npm run audit:docs`, in the CI docs job, runs `bridge audit apps/docs-site/src --baseline bridge-site-after.json --no-regress --fail-under 95`. I checked locally that both fail on an injected raw value.
- **Adoption page.** Two apps sit side by side, each showing before and after: "Admin demo (react-admin, migrated from MUI)" (untouched) and "Bridge itself (dogfooding)". Each app has its own trend.

### Audit, Bridge docs site

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token adoption | 9.7% (281 refs, 2628 hardcoded, 1932 `--br-*` refs) | 99.96%, shown as 100% (4667 refs, 2 hardcoded) |
| Component adoption | 52.8% (47 of 89) | 100% (210 of 210 scanned instances) |

The audit does not tell the whole story:
- **The 2 hardcoded values left** are `#000000` defaults of the color-picker `<input type="color">` in the token editor scripts. They are data, not styling.
- **The audit only reads CSS, TS and TSX.** Astro templates and HTML strings built by scripts are not scanned. Native controls in `.astro` files went from 178 to about 60, mostly `details` disclosures, the palette `dialog`, range and checkbox inputs, and selects filled by scripts. innerHTML templates in `src/scripts` still hold about 76 native elements: Reviews, History, the explorer detail panel and inline edit. - [x] Tier 2, medium: new component, variant or prop (additive). Opened as draft until design review

## Checks run locally

## Visual QA

Before is production, after is the local build. Shots cover Home, Color, Button, Studio overview, Studio tokens and Reviews, in light and dark at 1440, plus Home and Tokens at 390. Expected visual differences:

pr.body:
## Bridge v1: design system as code, end to end

Agent-authored integration of all Bridge work (Claude Code). **Risk tier 3**: adds and restructures tokens, renames packages to `@bridge-ds/*`, touches `.github/`. Needs design and tech review. Humans merge.

### What's in it
- **Design system**: tiered DTCG tokens (primitives, brands bridge/ocean, semantic light/dark, density, components), contrast gate (220 checks, 0 failing), 46 React components on Base UI, design language doc, Vitest + axe tests.
- **Bridge web platform** (`apps/docs-site`): token explorer with editing (every edit becomes a PR), Reviews (approve, request changes, merge with governance rules), History with revert planner, Branches, Adoption, Connect your Claude (MCP).
- **DS Bridge Figma plugin**: Pull (code to Figma) and Push (Figma to PR), tiered collections, contrast column fixed (the bug seen on #4).
- **MCP server + CLI** (`@bridge-ds/mcp`, `@bridge-ds/cli`): 21 tools for the user's own Claude, read-only without a token, never pushes to main.
- **Visual impact**: before/after/diff screenshots of impacted stories and app screens, posted on PRs.
- **Adoption audit**: `bridge audit`, Stylelint and ESLint plugins.
- **Branch previews**: snapshot packages per PR (pkg.pr.new), Vercel configs, staging token override. One-time setup in `docs/PREVIEWS.md`.
- **Demo product** (`apps/admin`): react-admin e-commerce demo (MIT, credited) migrated from MUI to Bridge, two fictional shops. Audit: tokens 0% to 100%, components 0% to 90.2% (remaining gaps listed in `apps/admin/DS-GAPS.md`).

### Checks run locally
tokens:build, typecheck, lint:css, admin:lint:css, npm test (327), mcp:test (68), plugin test (13) + build, plugins:build, build:packages (8), admin build, build-storybook, docs:build, `bridge check`, MCP stdio smoke test.

### Reviewer focus
- `.github/workflows/*` (new jobs: visual impact, preview packages, release which is inert without `NPM_TOKEN`).
- Package scope rename `@bridge-ds/*` (not published yet).
- Badge default is now subtle; Tooltip has no `role="tooltip"` (Base UI 1.9 behaviour).

### Not done / known limits
- Web write actions (approve, merge, propose) not yet exercised against GitHub.
- Overlay component previews in docs show only the trigger.
- Packages not published on npm; previews need the setup in `docs/PREVIEWS.md`.

Data display: Card restyled as a flat plate with an `interactive` option and padding sizes; Badge gains `appearance` (subtle, now the default, or solid), a dot, icons and sizes (existing solid badges must pass `appearance="solid"` to keep their look); new Avatar and AvatarGroup, Table (sortable headers with aria-sort, selectable rows, sticky header, focusable scroll region, useTableSort), Accordion, Tag (removable, toggleable), Divider and Kbd. Adds avatar, tag, kbd, divider and accordion component tokens.

Feedback: Alert (five tones, actions, dismiss, correct live region), Toast (ToastProvider and useToast with success, error, warning, info, promise, update and close), Progress (linear and circular, determinate and indeterminate), Skeleton, EmptyState, plus Spinner stories and guidance. Adds alert and skeleton component tokens.

Overlays: Dialog (sizes, scrolling body, footer, close last in focus order), AlertDialog (destructive confirmations, async confirm), Drawer (start, end, bottom with swipe), Popover, Tooltip with TooltipProvider, Menu (icons, shortcuts, groups, submenus, checkbox and radio items, danger items). Every popup carries the theme, brand and density scope. Adds menu and drawer component tokens.

Bridge token system v1. Adds a brand mapping layer (`bridge` default, `ocean` alternate) between primitives and semantic tokens, a component tier (button, input, checkbox, switch, slider, card, popup, dialog, tooltip, toast, table, tabs, progress, nav), comfortable and compact density, motion durations and easings with a reduced-motion override, layers (z-index), icon sizes, breakpoints, a 1.2 type scale from 14px with tracking tokens, and self-hosted IBM Plex Sans and Mono (`@bridge-ds/tokens/fonts.css`). Primitives are regenerated in OKLCH on one lightness ladder. The build now writes `dist/resolved.json` and fails when any pair in `contrast.checks.json` drops below its WCAG minimum in any brand and theme. Fixes `color.border.strong` against `color.surface.default` (now at least 3:1 in both themes).
Add usage guidance files for Button, Input, Badge and Card, plus the list of color pairs to check for contrast. They feed the new documentation site; no visual or API change.

body.title: A design lead can sign in by email, and the proxy keeps a lead's words to leads
body.body:
Stacked on #955. Security-sensitive, so kept small.

## What it does

- **Role:** `lead` on the email member record, given by an admin (`set-lead`, GitHub or email admin), in Settings, Members. Not for Can view. Read from the record on every request, never from the browser.
- **Email lead:** the proxy (`api/contribute`) treats them as able to act on any exploration of the team without owning it: pull request body, labels, comments, the developers' task, and in the library the note Done exploring removes. No push to someone's exploration in a copy. Nothing Bridge keeps about who it belongs to moves. So they run the same core functions as a GitHub lead, and writes go out as the app.
- **Hand over:** a new `exploration-keeper` action in `api/contribute`, for a lead by their record. The shared code moved to `api/_lib/exploration-keeper.ts`.
- **Gate for everyone else through Bridge** (`api/_lib/lead-gate.ts`): a lead's decision, `leadOkBy`, and on a team with design owners Done exploring, the `ready-for-devs` label and the developers' task answer 403 `lead-only`. Read against the body on GitHub.
- **Email and Home:** what waits on a lead also goes to email leads. Home gives them the row.

## A difference from the brief

The brief asked for an endpoint where the server writes for GitHub leads and email leads alike. I did not build that:

- The API does not import core, so running Looks right on the server would mean a second copy of the hand-off.
- The proxy already holds the deny-by-default policy and the app identity, so the check fits there with far less code.
- A GitHub lead has write access, so a server check for them would add no protection: they, and anyone with write, can edit on GitHub directly.

So GitHub leads keep writing with their own token, unchecked by Bridge.

## What stays bypassable

- Anyone with write access on GitHub (repository or copy) can edit the pull request body, labels and tasks directly. That includes GitHub leads and admins.
- GitHub designers on the library keep their own GitHub path, so the gate does not apply there.
- Anyone in Studio on a team with no `governance.owners.design`: Done exploring needs nobody.

## Limits

- A team whose only leads are email leads does not get the lead step: Studio decides from `owners.design`, so it goes straight to the developers. Say if this should change.
- An owner entry that names a GitHub team counts as an owner for the gate. Fine, since the client expands it the same way.
- A task an email lead files is recorded as theirs, so a developer's question on it notifies them, not the designer. Not fixed here.
- "Reviewer stays GitHub" in `docs/GOVERNANCE.md` was not touched and stays true for code approval.

body.title: perf(studio): slim pull request lists in the read proxy
body.body:
## What changed and why

Agent-authored. The Studio home waits on lists of pull requests. The weight is not the bodies (about 10 percent of the list) but the two full repository objects GitHub repeats in every pull request, plus API links on every person and label. `pulls?state=all&per_page=50` (core `listPullRequests('all')`, read for suggestions) weighed 1042 KB, over `MAX_KEPT_CHARS` (700 000), so it was never kept: every read was an `x-bridge-cache: miss` that paid GitHub 0.8 to 1.2 s, and it holds the home's `loading` state.

- `api/_lib/slim-pulls.ts`: the proxy keeps and answers `/pulls` lists without what no page reads. It is the server copy of core `trimGitHub`, which already serves these same lists to the public demo teams; a test holds the two equal. **Bodies are not touched**, so exploration blocks and requester lines stay byte for byte. `head.repo` stays null on a deleted fork. One pull request (`/pulls/N`) and its parts stay whole.
- Slimmed lists live under their own Redis keys, so a whole list kept before this is never answered or confirmed by ETag.
- Lists answer `private, no-cache` instead of `private, no-store`: the browser keeps them and asks again each time, so freshness is unchanged and an unchanged list costs a 304. Authorisation still runs on every read. Every other read stays `no-store`.

Per-item reads were not touched: they are already parallel and do not hold first paint (`designTaskReads`, `readXpFiles`, `taskRead`).
